say.text: The Recruit is a levy of the Tikrit garrison: an invented person, who stood on the landing the day the boats were lent.
My lord. Before the day of the boats I had never tasted bread from the citadel's granary.
No one had. It was kept for a siege.
The men in the ranks said the governor would have our heads for opening it to Zengi's people.
Ayyub gave the fugitives boats, kindness and provisions; Bihruz sent him a letter of blame.
The governor wrote me a letter. That was all it cost.
And if they had been the Caliph's men, who came to the river hungry?
The same. It was never about whose they were. A man with nothing in his hands is a guest.
Then I know what a garrison is for, my lord. I will remember where I learned it.
Learn the other half as well: how to hold a landing. We shall want both.
